hints: Look at the longest carbon chain first and spot the two functional features, the C=C double bond and the OH group.
Try numbering the six-carbon chain from the end nearest the OH group, this gives the OH position 2 and the double bond starting at 3.
Check whether the double bond needs its own locant number and whether the two larger groups are opposite each other across the C=C.
walkthrough:
**Find the parent chain**

Great start, let's count together. The continuous chain through the double bond and the carbon bearing OH has six carbons, so the parent is hexene.

$$\text{6 carbons + one C=C = hexene}$$

**Number to give the OH the lowest locant**

The OH group gets priority for low numbering. Number from the right (the $\text{CH}_3$ end near OH).

$$\text{C1 (CH}_3) - \text{C2 (CH-OH)} - \text{C3 = C4} - \text{C5} - \text{C6}$$

**Add both locants**

This gives OH on C2 and the double bond starting on C3. We must show both positions, so we get 2-hydroxyhex-3-ene.

$$\text{2-hydroxy + hex-3-ene}$$

**Assign cis-trans**

Look across the C=C. The carbon chains continue on opposite sides of the double bond, one to the left and one up to the right. That is the trans (E) arrangement, so the full name is trans-2-hydroxyhex-3-ene.

options.A: Correct and complete. Numbering from the OH end gives the lowest locants, OH at 2 and C=C at 3, plus the trans geometry. This matches the structure of compound X exactly.
options.B: Close but incomplete. It has the correct OH position and trans label, but it misses the locant for the double bond. In IUPAC naming for this syllabus you must state where the C=C starts, which is hex-3-ene, not just hexene.
options.C: This numbers from the wrong end. Numbering from the left gives OH at 5, but the rule is to give the OH group (the principal substituent here) the lowest possible number, so 2 is correct, not 5.
options.D: This has two errors. It numbers from the wrong end giving 5 instead of 2, and it also omits the locant 3 for the double bond. Always number to give OH the lowest number and include the ene position.
